title: Signal Conditioning: Bridges, Amplifiers and Analog Filters

contract.reader: An engineering student or engineer comfortable with basic circuit analysis who must connect a small sensor signal to an ADC
contract.problem: Designing the analog front end between a sensor and a converter: excitation, bridge, amplification, current and charge conversion, filtering and protection
contract.outcome: Choose excitation and lead-wire connections, compute bridge outputs and nonlinearity, use op-amp and instrumentation-amplifier gain and CMRR, convert current and charge, choose a filter order, and assemble a ratiometric load-cell channel
contract.contribution: Follows one signal through the five jobs of conditioning in order and closes with a complete, numerically consistent load-cell channel that the next entries digitize, budget and calibrate
contract.evidence: Worked numbers in the text; two generated figures (bridge, Butterworth responses); Fraden (2016), Franco (2015), Horowitz and Hill (2015), Pallas-Areny and Webster (2001)
contract.limitations: Ideal circuits plus a list of imperfections; no schematics of the amplifier circuits; no noise budget (left to the next entries)

findings.problem: No schematic of the three-op-amp instrumentation amplifier or the virtual-ground converters, and no block diagram of the Section 7 channel; all are described in words or connection tables.
findings.whyItMatters: These circuits are the article's main content, and the ratiometric connection of Section 7 is easiest to grasp as one supply feeding both bridge and ADC reference.
findings.action: Add, via scripts/generate-diagrams.py, an in-amp schematic (R, R_G, reference terminal labeled as in the text) and a block diagram of the Section 7 channel, with captions saying what to notice.
findings.acceptance: On new captures the in-amp schematic appears in 4.1 and the channel diagram in Section 7, legible at 1280 and 360 px and in dark mode, with labels matching the text.

findings.location: Section 2.1 bridge figure and equation (mobile-light-08, 09); Section 6.2 Butterworth figure and order table (mobile-light-32, 33; mobile-dark-32)
findings.problem: At 360 px the bridge figure's R3/V_B side and the bridge equation's subtracted R4/(R3 + R4) are hidden; the Butterworth figure's 'first order' and 'second order' labels are off-screen and the rest about 6 px high; the '|H| at 3 Hz' column, which the next paragraph introduces as 'the last column', is under the scroll shadow.
findings.whyItMatters: A phone reader cannot see the second divider, tell the curves apart or read the numbers the paragraph discusses.
findings.action: Split the bridge equation over two lines; label the Butterworth curves inside the plot or in the caption at a legible size; drop or merge the Attenuation column so the 3 Hz column fits.
findings.acceptance: At 360 px the full bridge equation is visible, all three Butterworth curves are identifiable from legible labels, and the 3 Hz column is visible without scrolling.
